literal: Even the weak, having become strong, will conquer, place having known, at the enemies, having protected, if they act.
translation: Even the weak will gather strength and conquer their foes, if they choose the right place, protect themselves, and then act.
modern: தக்க இடத்தினை அறிந்து, தம்மைக் காத்துக்கொண்டு பகைவரிடம் போர் செய்தால், வலிமையற்றவர்களும் வலிமை பெற்று வெல்வார்கள்.
explanation: This couplet explains the strategic advantage of choosing the right battleground. The word 'இடன்' (place) is central, emphasizing that location can compensate for a lack of inherent power. If even weak people ('ஆற்றாரும்') carefully protect themselves ('போற்றி') and engage their enemies in a well-chosen place, they will gather strength ('ஆற்றி') and achieve victory ('அடுப'). It highlights that tactical positioning and self-defense are just as crucial as raw strength.
